title: Charge-sharing-resistant advanced-node storage latches
open: Can a storage latch at advanced technology nodes preserve its data when a high-LET particle strike deposits charge at multiple nodes simultaneously, without paying an impractical cost in area, delay, or power? A complete answer must demonstrate the protection holds across strike angles, supply voltage, temperature, and realistic physical layouts.
status: Charge sharing has challenged scaling for decades. Heavy-ion tests in 2025 of 14-nm FinFET flip-flops found interleaved redundancy effective, while conventional DICE protection degraded at high LET. Key work: Hai-song Li et al. (2025), [*Investigation of DFF cells SEU effect for 14 nm bulk silicon FinFET technology irradiated by heavy ions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115857).
solved_when: A latch design is shown — by measurement or simulation on realistic layouts — to retain stored data under multi-node charge collection from high-LET strikes over varied strike angles, voltages, and temperatures, while meeting practical area, delay, and power budgets.
why: Logical redundancy built into a latch need not survive disturbances that are physically correlated, so the dominant hardening techniques of previous nodes can silently fail at advanced nodes.
key_works: Hai-song Li et al. (2025), [*Investigation of DFF cells SEU effect for 14 nm bulk silicon FinFET technology irradiated by heavy ions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115857).

title: NEM relay contacts with stable loaded-switching lifetimes
open: Can nanoelectromechanical relay contacts be made to keep low resistance and release repeatably through prolonged switching of realistic capacitive loads? The goal is to quantify and suppress the competing effects of adhesion, wear, oxidation, and microwelding at the small contact forces these devices require.
status: The contact problem has been central to NEM logic proposals since the 2000s. In 2026, mechanical shock and vibration testing by Ivan Marozau et al. ([*Mechanical shock and vibration testing of volatile and non-volatile nanoelectromechanical switches*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115980)) preserved mechanical function but revealed contact-related electrical variability and wear of the gold coating, showing that mechanical survival alone does not establish switching lifetime.
solved_when: Relay contacts demonstrate low, stable resistance and repeatable release throughout prolonged loaded switching of realistic capacitive loads, with the degradation mechanisms of adhesion, wear, oxidation, and microwelding quantified and suppressed at small contact forces.
why: Contact degradation can defeat the energy advantage that NEM relays gain from essentially zero off-state leakage, so without stable contacts the technology's core benefit is lost.
key_works: Ivan Marozau et al. (2026), [*Mechanical shock and vibration testing of volatile and non-volatile nanoelectromechanical switches*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115980).

title: Buried EUV-mask phase-defect inspection
open: Can buried defects in the multilayer stack of an EUV mask be detected, localized, and assessed for printability at production throughput — even when a patterned absorber or pellicle hides them from view?
status: Nancale optical detection and phase-sensitive techniques have progressed for over a decade. A 2013 NIST study by Attota and Jindal, ["Through-focus scanning optical microscopy for defect inspection of EUV masks"](https://www.nist.gov/publications/through-focus-scanning-optical-microscopy-defect-inspection-euv-masks), demonstrated useful defect discrimination, but not exhaustive production inspection.
solved_when: An inspection method reliably detects and localizes buried multilayer defects, judges their printability, and operates at production throughput, including cases obscured by patterned absorbers or pellicles.
why: A single invisible mask defect is replicated across every waer printed from that mask, so missing it silently multiplies yield loss; reliable buried-defect inspection prevents that duplication.
key_works: Attota and Jindal (2013), [“Through-focus scanning optical microscopy for defect inspection of EUV masks”](https://www.nist.gov/publications/through-focus-scanning-optical-microscopy-defect-inspection-euv-masks).

title: Fast conformal deposition in deep closed-end features
open: Can we achieve uniform thickness and composition throughout increasingly deep closed-end features without exposure and purge times long enough to make deposition economically unviable?
status: ALD is already highly conformal, but the unresolved scaling trade-off couples precursor transport, sticking, depletion, and radical recombination; this coupling was systematized by Cremers, Puurunen, and Dendooven (2019), ["Conformality in atomic layer deposition: Current status overview of analysis and modelling"](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5060967).
solved_when: A deposition process demonstrably maintains uniform thickness and composition across deep closed-end features while keeping exposure and purge times within economically acceptable limits, with the precursor transport, sticking, depletion, and radical recombination trade-offs quantified.
why: It underpins reliable capacitors, memory channels, and three-dimensional gate stacks, whose performance depends directly on conformality in deep structures.
key_works: Cremers, Puurunen, and Dendooven (2019), [“Conformality in atomic layer deposition: Current status overview of analysis and modelling”](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5060967).

title: Glitch-power prediction across workloads and technologies
open: Can glitch power — the energy burned by narrow pulses and hazards in combinational logic — be predicted fast enough for large designs, while accounting for correlated input timing and realistic workloads, without resorting to transistor-level simulation of every transition?
status: A 2024 study by Villegas and Vourkas, ["A Gate-Level Power Estimation Approach with a Comprehensive Definition of Thresholds for Classification and Filtering of Inertial Glitch Pulses"](https://doi.org/10.3390/jlpea14030041), improved cell-specific pulse filtering in 32 nm simulations; accurate transfer across libraries, operating points, and large heterogeneous designs remains the target.
solved_when: An estimation method accurately predicts glitch energy across libraries, operating points, and large heterogeneous designs at large-design speed, incorporating correlated input timing and realistic workloads, with accuracy matching the level achieved by cell-specific pulse filtering in 32 nm simulations.
why: It makes power budgets and optimization decisions reflect the physical switching activity that actually occurs in silicon, rather than idealized transition counts.
key_works: Villegas and Vourkas (2024), [“A Gate-Level Power Estimation Approach with a Comprehensive Definition of Thresholds for Classification and Filtering of Inertial Glitch Pulses”](https://doi.org/10.3390/jlpea14030041).

title: Transferable and reproducible learned chip placement
open: Can a learned chip placer beat strong conventional baselines on designs and technologies it has never seen, with results that reproduce across repeated runs? More precisely: under what conditions, accounting for training cost and post-route metrics, does a learned placer's advantage hold on genuinely out-of-distribution benchmarks?
status: Mirhoseini et al. reported successful deployment in 2021; independent open assessments (Cheng et al., 2023) and a 2024 addendum show why the evaluation protocol and transfer claims need explicit evidence.
solved_when: A learned placer is shown, under an evaluation protocol with explicit evidence of transfer, to outperform strong conventional baselines on genuinely unseen designs and technologies — with training cost and post-route metrics reported and results reproducible across repeated runs.
why: It separates reusable design intelligence from benchmark-specific optimization: only genuine transfer makes a learned placer a dependable tool rather than a tuned artifact.
key_works: Mirhoseini et al. (2021), [“A graph placement methodology for fast chip design”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03544-w); Cheng et al. (2023), [“Assessment of Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11014).

title: Masking proofs that survive physical implementation
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Can we build composable leakage-security proofs for masked circuits that remain valid when confronted with the measured behavior of real CMOS hardware — glitches, unequal wire delays, signal coupling, and process variation — while keeping implementation overhead affordable? Formally, the goal is a masking scheme and proof framework in the robust probing setting whose leakage model provably covers these physical defaults as they actually manifest in fabricated devices.
status: Robust probing models have solved important formal subproblems; an analysis by Müller, Lammers, and Moradi (2024), ["A Deep Analysis of two Glitch-Free Hardware Masking Schemes SESYM and LMDPL"](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/035), demonstrates why eliminating glitches alone does not settle delay-induced leakage. Foundational composable treatment: Faust et al. (2017/2018), ["Composable Masking Schemes in the Presence of Physical Defaults and the Robust Probing Model"](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/711).
solved_when: A composable masking proof (robust probing model or successor) is shown sound against experimentally characterized CMOS effects — glitches, unequal delays, coupling, and process variation — with an implementation whose overhead is demonstrably affordable.
why: It would give cryptographic hardware security guarantees that match how fabricated circuits actually behave, rather than idealized models that real devices violate.
key_works: Faust et al. (2017/2018), [“Composable Masking Schemes in the Presence of Physical Defaults and the Robust Probing Model”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/711); Müller, Lammers, and Moradi (2024), [“A Deep Analysis of two Glitch-Free Hardware Masking Schemes SESYM and LMDPL”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/035).

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave electrically injected group-IV laser
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Can a group-IV semiconductor laser run continuously under electrical injection at room temperature and deliver its light into an on-chip waveguide? The goal is a GeSn/SiGeSn device, co-integrated with silicon, that lases efficiently and sustains operation without cryogenic cooling.
status: Pursued since the 1990s. Optical pumping and pulsed electrical operation establish partial feasibility, and Seidel and colleagues demonstrated continuous-wave electrically pumped lasing in 2024, but only up to 35 K [Seidel et al. (2024), *Continuous-wave electrically pumped multi-quantum-well laser based on group-IV semiconductors*, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54873-z].
solved_when: A room-temperature, continuous-wave, electrically injected GeSn/SiGeSn laser is demonstrated, coupled into a useful on-chip waveguide with efficient, sustained operation.
why: It completes a monolithic group-IV optical-source platform, removing the need for separately assembled III–V gain chips in silicon photonics.
key_works: Seidel et al. (2024), [*Continuous-wave electrically pumped multi-quantum-well laser based on group-IV semiconductors*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54873-z).
aliases: Electrically pumped silicon-compatible laser; group-IV laser temperature problem.

title: Manufacturable Pockels photonics with stable interfaces
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Can heterogeneous electro-optic photonics be built to combine low optical loss, low drive voltage, and high bandwidth, while also achieving uniform wafer-scale performance and bonded interfaces that remain stable over the full service life?
status: Effort accelerated during the 2010s. Wang and colleagues demonstrated wafer-scale lithium-tantalate photonics in 2024, extending the material options beyond lithium niobate; production-scale multimaterial yield and qualification remain combined challenges. Key work: Wang et al. (2024), [*Lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuits for volume manufacturing*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07369-1).
solved_when: Devices are demonstrated with simultaneously low optical loss, low drive voltage, high bandwidth, uniform wafer performance, and stable bonded interfaces over service life, at production scale with qualified multimaterial yield.
why: It would add efficient Pockels-effect modulation to silicon-based communication and sensing chips; without stable, manufacturable interfaces, the modulators cannot be integrated reliably into volume production.
key_works: Wang et al. (2024), [*Lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuits for volume manufacturing*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07369-1).

title: Lifetime lead containment after photovoltaic module damage
open: Can lead-containing photovoltaic modules be made to capture their own lead even after a lifetime of real-world abuse — decades of weathering combined with realistic cracking, fire, flooding, and recycling — without sacrificing performance or economical manufacture?
status: Lead leakage from damaged modules has been a concern since the 2010s. Chen and colleagues substantially reduced lead release from damaged mini-modules with ion-exchange resins in 2020 (Chen et al. (2020), [*Trapping lead in perovskite solar modules with abundant and low-cost cation-exchange resins*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-020-00716-2)); however, validation over module lifetimes and across realistic failure scenarios remains to be done at scale.
solved_when: A lead-capture strategy is demonstrated to remain effective after decades of weathering and realistic combinations of cracking, fire, flooding, and recycling, while preserving performance and economical manufacture.
why: It would enable safer deployment and end-of-life handling of lead-containing absorbers, removing the main environmental barrier to their field use.
key_works: Chen et al. (2020), [*Trapping lead in perovskite solar modules with abundant and low-cost cation-exchange resins*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-020-00716-2).

title: Durable narrow-bandgap tin–lead perovskite junctions
open: Can a complete tin–lead perovskite photovoltaic junction be made to survive the combined stresses of heat and illumination without degrading? Formally, the goal is to stabilize such junctions against self-doping, ionic redistribution, interfacial reactions, and oxidation under simultaneous thermal and optical stress, while preserving their narrow-bandgap efficiency.
status: A persistent 2010s–2020s problem. Rombach et al. (2025), [*Disentangling degradation pathways of narrow bandgap lead-tin perovskite material and photovoltaic devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58489-9), showed that dominant degradation pathways change with the hole-transport material, and that structurally stable absorbers can still yield deteriorating devices.
solved_when: A full tin–lead photovoltaic junction demonstrates stability against self-doping, ionic redistribution, interfacial reactions, and oxidation under simultaneous heat and illumination, without loss of narrow-bandgap efficiency.
why: Solving this unlocks durable all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics, where narrow-bandgap tin–lead junctions are the component that currently limits lifetime.
key_works: Rombach et al. (2025), [*Disentangling degradation pathways of narrow bandgap lead-tin perovskite material and photovoltaic devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58489-9).

title: Eliminating the kesterite voltage deficit
open: Can the voltage deficit that limits kesterite solar cells be eliminated by suppressing bulk and interface losses, without introducing compensating defects or sacrificing manufacturable phase purity?
status: Open since the 2000s. Magnesium-assisted ordering produced 14.9%-efficient certified cells in 2025 (Wang et al., 2025 online; 2026 issue, [*Vacancy-enhanced cation ordering via magnesium doping to enable kesterite solar cells with 14.9% certified efficiency*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01902-w)); defect activity and ordering kinetics remain intertwined.
solved_when: A kesterite cell demonstrates that its voltage deficit has been removed, with both bulk and interface recombination losses suppressed, no compensating defects introduced, and phase purity compatible with manufacturing preserved.
why: It would enable high-performance thin-film photovoltaics built from relatively abundant constituent elements.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025 online; 2026 issue), [*Vacancy-enhanced cation ordering via magnesium doping to enable kesterite solar cells with 14.9% certified efficiency*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01902-w).

title: Unambiguous non-Abelian Majorana operations in semiconductor hybrids
open: Can non-Abelian operations on Majorana modes in semiconductor–superconductor hybrid devices be demonstrated unambiguously — for example, by showing noncommuting exchange or equivalent measurement-only operations — while ruling out explanations based on ordinary Andreev bound states and establishing a protected operating regime?
status: Pursued since 2010-era nanowire proposals. Microsoft Azure Quantum's 2025 parity-readout experiment explicitly allowed trivial and topological interpretations; parity measurement alone is not non-Abelian braiding. Key work: Microsoft Azure Quantum and Aghaee et al. (2025), [*Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2).
solved_when: Noncommuting exchange (or equivalent measurement-only) operations on semiconductor–superconductor Majorana modes are experimentally demonstrated, with ordinary Andreev-state explanations excluded and a protected operating regime established.
why: It tests the physical basis of a proposed protected quantum-computing platform: without such a demonstration, the platform's core promise of topological protection rests on unverified physics.
key_works: Microsoft Azure Quantum and Aghaee et al. (2025), [*Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2).

title: Predicting coupled chemical degradation in blue OLEDs
open: Can we predict how a blue OLED's luminance decays over time — and what chemical products form — from the underlying electron-, exciton-, and mixed-carrier degradation reactions, without fitting each device's lifetime individually? In formal terms, is there a predictive model of the coupled degradation network that transfers across materials and operating conditions?
status: Open for decades. Kim et al. (2023), [*Critical role of electrons in the short lifetime of blue OLEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-43408-7), combined calculations, control devices, and mass spectrometry to identify electron-assisted degradation in iridium emitters, but prediction across materials and conditions remains unresolved.
solved_when: The model quantitatively predicts luminance decay curves and failure products for blue OLEDs across different emitter materials and driving conditions, with no per-device fitting of lifetime parameters.
why: It would replace empirical lifetime screening with a design tool, letting emitter chemistries be chosen for durability before devices are built and tested.
key_works: Kim et al. (2023), [*Critical role of electrons in the short lifetime of blue OLEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-43408-7).

title: High-brightness narrowband blue OLEDs without triplet accumulation
open: Can a sensitized deep-blue OLED hold a narrow emission spectrum and high efficiency at sustained high luminance without succumbing to triplet accumulation and the damage it causes? Formally, can trapping, triplet accumulation, exciton annihilation, and chemical degradation all be suppressed simultaneously in a narrowband blue emitter operating at high brightness?
status: The problem has been pursued since the 2010s. Fan et al. (2025) [*Stable narrowband blue OLEDs by modulating frontier molecular orbital levels*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60172-y) shifted molecular orbital energies, obtaining 13-nm emission bandwidth and approximately 20% efficiency at 1,000 cd/m², but high-brightness lifetime remains challenging.
solved_when: A sensitized blue emitter demonstrates a narrow deep-blue spectrum (on the order of 13-nm bandwidth) with efficiency around 20% or higher at 1,000 cd/m², sustained under high-brightness operation with triplet accumulation, annihilation, and chemical degradation suppressed over a practical lifetime.
why: It would enable colour-pure, power-efficient displays that survive demanding luminance requirements — currently the narrowband blue emitters degrade or lose efficiency exactly when driven hardest.
key_works: Fan et al. (2025), [*Stable narrowband blue OLEDs by modulating frontier molecular orbital levels*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60172-y).

title: Comparable lifecycle inventories per good die
open: Can the community establish comparable lifecycle inventories for semiconductor fabrication, normalized per yielding functional die rather than per wafer? Such inventories would cover energy, water, chemicals, and emissions, and account for equipment utilization, process yield, packaging, and uncertainty.
status: Lifecycle frameworks and virtual-fab models exist; imec (2025), ["How can we reduce environmental impact in chip manufacturing?"](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/how-can-we-reduce-environmental-impact-chip-manufacturing), explicitly notes dependence on yield, utilization, die size, and other assumptions.
solved_when: Auditable inventories are published with all of the listed elements — energy, water, chemical, and emissions flows normalized to yielding functional dies, together with equipment utilization, process yield, packaging, and quantified uncertainty — enabling meaningful cross-fabrication-route comparison.
why: Without die-level normalization that includes yield and utilization, published footprints are not comparable, and design or process choices cannot be evaluated on their true environmental cost; with it, fabrication routes and design choices can be compared meaningfully.
key_works: imec (2025), [“How can we reduce environmental impact in chip manufacturing?”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/how-can-we-reduce-environmental-impact-chip-manufacturing).

title: Predictive charged-defect energetics
open: Can we predict the formation free energies of charged point defects in semiconductors, and their charge-transition levels, with reliable, transferable uncertainty estimates? The prediction must hold blind against independently identified defects, covering localized defect states, competing structural geometries, and realistic chemical-potential conditions.
status: A decades-old problem. Finite-size corrections and hybrid functionals have substantially improved the accuracy of first-principles defect calculations, yet defect-specific validation of any computational prediction remains necessary. Key work: C. Freysoldt et al. (2014), [First-principles calculations for point defects in solids](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.253).
solved_when: A method achieves blind agreement with independently identified defects across semiconductor families, while reporting transferable uncertainty estimates on defect formation free energies and charge-transition levels, with treatment of localized states, competing geometries, and realistic chemical potentials.
why: It would make doping and carrier-lifetime engineering less empirical by grounding design decisions in quantitatively trusted defect predictions.
key_works: C. Freysoldt et al. (2014), [First-principles calculations for point defects in solids](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.253).

title: Multimode anharmonic nonradiative capture
open: Can we compute carrier-capture rates for defects when many vibrational modes, anharmonic potentials, tunnelling, and strong electronic coupling all act at once — and can we say, with experimental validation, when the usual single-coordinate picture breaks down?
status: The problem is decades old. Calculations by A. Alkauskas, Q. Yan, and C. G. Van de Walle (2014), [First-principles theory of nonradiative carrier capture via multiphonon emission](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.90.075202), quantitatively described selected GaN and ZnO defects, but broader multimode and anharmonic cases remain unresolved.
solved_when: A theoretical framework yields quantitative capture rates for multimode anharmonic defects that match experiment, together with validated criteria delimiting the failure of single-coordinate approximations.
why: It identifies which rare defects actually dominate recombination, and thus which defects matter for device performance rather than being masked by approximations.
key_works: A. Alkauskas, Q. Yan, and C. G. Van de Walle (2014), [First-principles theory of nonradiative carrier capture via multiphonon emission](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.90.075202).

title: Spatial hot-phonon bottleneck inversion
open: Can we reconstruct the local carrier and phonon distributions inside a photoexcited semiconductor from measurement, without confusing spatial transport with genuine changes in the spectra? More precisely, can a transferable microscopic inversion predict whether phonon reabsorption drives the carrier profile to expand, contract (apparent negative diffusion), or become non-Gaussian?
status: A longstanding problem. In 2024, transient-microscopy experiments on monolayer MoS₂ resolved carrier expansion, an apparent negative-diffusion regime, and subsequent expansion, but a transferable microscopic inversion remains open. Key work: X. Wei et al. (2024), [Unveiling Spatiotemporal Diffusion of Hot Carriers Influenced by Spatial Nonuniform Hot Phonon Bottleneck Effect in Monolayer MoS2](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c02059).
solved_when: A transferable microscopic inversion framework recovers local carrier and phonon distributions from spatiotemporal data and correctly predicts the observed regimes — expansion, apparent negative diffusion, and subsequent expansion — such as those seen in monolayer MoS₂.
why: It would replace misleading single-temperature descriptions of energy flow with a quantitatively faithful picture of coupled carrier–phonon dynamics.
key_works: X. Wei et al. (2024), [Unveiling Spatiotemporal Diffusion of Hot Carriers Influenced by Spatial Nonuniform Hot Phonon Bottleneck Effect in Monolayer MoS2](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c02059).

title: The Ta2NiSe5 excitonic order parameter
open: Does electron–hole pairing drive the structural transition in Ta₂NiSe₅, merely follow the lattice distortion, or do electronic and lattice orders form an inseparable cooperative state? A decisive experiment must discriminate among these scenarios rather than simply observe a gap.
status: The excitonic-insulator proposal dates to the 1960s, and as of 2025 measurements still address competing electronic and lattice interpretations, e.g. N. Maraytta et al. (2025), [Unveiling excitonic insulator signatures in Ta2NiSe5 through structural and orbital probes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-20909-7).
solved_when: An experiment conclusively distinguishes exciton-driven, lattice-driven, and cooperative-order interpretations of the Ta₂NiSe₅ transition beyond gap observation.
why: It establishes when excitonic insulation is a distinct thermodynamic phase, rather than an epiphenomenon of lattice distortion.
key_works: N. Maraytta et al. (2025), [Unveiling excitonic insulator signatures in Ta2NiSe5 through structural and orbital probes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-20909-7).

title: Carrier-mediated ferromagnetism in dilute wide-gap nitrides
open: Can a dilute magnetic wide-gap nitride be grown in which ferromagnetism is genuinely carrier-mediated, reproducible, and survives above room temperature — with precipitates and secondary phases rigorously excluded — and can its exchange mechanism be pinned down with complementary probes?
status: Pursued since around 2000; established low-temperature functionalities do not establish this combined high-temperature target. Key works: T. Dietl and H. Ohno (2014), [Dilute ferromagnetic semiconductors: Physics and spintronic structures](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.187); [arXiv:1307.3429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3429).
solved_when: A homogeneous dilute magnetic nitride exhibits reproducible ferromagnetism above room temperature, the magnetism is shown to be controlled by electrical carriers, secondary phases and precipitates are excluded, and complementary experimental probes agree on the exchange mechanism.
why: It would connect electrical carrier control with robust magnetic functionality, the prerequisite for practical semiconductor spintronic devices.
key_works: T. Dietl and H. Ohno (2014), [Dilute ferromagnetic semiconductors: Physics and spintronic structures](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.187); [arXiv:1307.3429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3429).

title: Affordable native GaN substrates
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Can native GaN substrates be produced at larger wafer sizes, with low defect density, controlled conductivity, and usable yield, at a cost low enough to support widespread adoption of vertical GaN devices?
status: Commercial GaN substrates exist, but cost and quality barriers persist; these were noted in the 2018 roadmap and remain in a 2026 assessment. Key works: H. Amano et al. (2018), [The 2018 GaN power electronics roadmap](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6463/aaaf9d); R. Shankari et al. (2026), [Vertical gallium nitride MOSFETs: Advanced architectures, fabrication technologies, and performance breakthroughs for high-power applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mee.2025.112418).
solved_when: Larger native GaN wafers are produced with low defect density, controlled conductivity, and usable yield at costs supporting widespread vertical devices.
why: Native substrates reduce defects and mismatch in vertical structures, enabling practical vertical GaN power devices.
key_works: H. Amano et al. (2018), [The 2018 GaN power electronics roadmap](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6463/aaaf9d); R. Shankari et al. (2026), [Vertical gallium nitride MOSFETs: Advanced architectures, fabrication technologies, and performance breakthroughs for high-power applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mee.2025.112418).

title: Useful p-type beta-Ga2O3
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Can beta-Ga2O3 be made to conduct via mobile holes at densities and mobilities useful for devices, or can the field establish firm practical limits from hole self-trapping and compensation?
status: This is a longstanding open problem; a 2024 review establishes that beta-Ga2O3 has no useful bipolar conductivity. Related considerations include small-polaron localization and thermodynamic dopability limits in oxide chemistry, as discussed in J. L. Lyons, D. Wickramaratne, and A. Janotti (2024), [Dopants and defects in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cossms.2024.101148).
solved_when: Reproducible p-type (mobile-hole) transport is demonstrated with useful carrier density and mobility, or a practical quantitative account of self-trapping and compensation limits shows such transport is unattainable.
why: Useful p-type beta-Ga2O3 would enable native p–n junction functionality in this ultrawide-gap oxide.
key_works: J. L. Lyons, D. Wickramaratne, and A. Janotti (2024), [Dopants and defects in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cossms.2024.101148).

title: Atomic assignment of electrically active Ga2O3 defects
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Can the electrically active defect trap families measured in Ga₂O₃ be assigned to specific atomic-scale structures — vacancies, impurity atoms, complexes, and local structural variants — together with their charge states and capture cross-sections? A complete answer would reconcile the spectroscopic signatures, first-principles calculations, growth chemistry, and irradiation results within a single consistent picture.
status: The problem has been active since electronic-grade Ga₂O₃ emerged; McCluskey's 2020 tutorial ([Point defects in Ga2O3](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5142195)) documents both established defect behavior and the assignments that remain incomplete; his publication list is at [labs.wsu.edu/mccluskey/publications/articles2020](https://labs.wsu.edu/mccluskey/publications/articles2020/).
solved_when: Each measured trap family is attributed to a specific defect (vacancy, impurity, complex, or local structure) with identified charge state and capture cross-section, and the assignment is consistent across spectroscopy, calculations, growth chemistry, and irradiation data.
why: It enables reproducible compensation and leakage control in Ga₂O₃ devices.
key_works: M. D. McCluskey (2020), [Point defects in Ga2O3](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5142195); [author publication list](https://labs.wsu.edu/mccluskey/publications/articles2020/).

title: Stable low-resistance contacts to n-type diamond
open: Can we fabricate electron-injecting contacts to n-type diamond that stay uniform and low-resistance under sustained high temperature and high current — and, in doing so, experimentally distinguish contact-limited injection barriers from bulk donor freeze-out?
status: The problem is decades old. Elevated-temperature n-channel device demonstrations, notably Liao et al. (2024), [High-Temperature and High-Electron Mobility Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors Based on N-Type Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202306013), still leave substantial injection and bulk-resistance constraints unresolved.
solved_when: A contact technology demonstrates uniform, stable electron injection to n-type diamond under high-temperature, high-current operation, with measurements that separate contact barrier effects from bulk donor freeze-out and show contacts no longer dominating device resistance.
why: Without such contacts, contact resistance dominates power losses in n-type diamond devices, masking the material's intrinsic high-temperature capability.
key_works: Liao et al. (2024), [High-Temperature and High-Electron Mobility Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors Based on N-Type Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202306013).

title: Efficient bulk p-type AlN
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Can bulk aluminum nitride be made to conduct holes reproducibly and efficiently? That is, can a doped bulk AlN crystal achieve adequate acceptor activation and low compensation while preserving crystal quality, with the actual transport mechanism identified?
status: Pursued for decades; a 2024 review (T. Wostatek et al., [Ammonothermal Crystal Growth of Functional Nitrides for Semiconductor Devices: Status and Potential](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17133104)) describes renewed Be-doping progress alongside incorporation, acceptor-depth, and solubility constraints.
solved_when: Bulk hole conduction in AlN is demonstrated reproducibly, with adequate activation, low compensation, preserved crystal quality, and an identified transport mechanism.
why: It unlocks bipolar ultrawide-gap nitride structures built on AlN.
key_works: T. Wostatek et al. (2024), [Ammonothermal Crystal Growth of Functional Nitrides for Semiconductor Devices: Status and Potential](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17133104).

title: Polarization-free high-flux CdZnTe
open: Can thick CdZnTe detectors be made to keep uniform electric fields, stable charge collection, and low leakage current under intense irradiation? Formally, the goal is a construction that suppresses both bias-induced and radiation-induced trap charging over large detector areas.
status: The problem has been studied for decades; high-flux material and 2024 XIDer experiments have improved performance, but trapping and time-dependent leakage persist (M. Collonge et al. (2024), [Probing the potential of CdZnTe for high-energy high-flux 2D X-ray detection using the XIDer incremental digital integrating readout](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphy.2024.1304570)).
solved_when: A CdZnTe detector design demonstrates uniform fields, stable charge collection, and low leakage under intense irradiation, with control of both bias-induced and radiation-induced trap charging maintained over large areas.
why: It would enable detectors for intense next-generation light sources.
key_works: M. Collonge et al. (2024), [Probing the potential of CdZnTe for high-energy high-flux 2D X-ray detection using the XIDer incremental digital integrating readout](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphy.2024.1304570).

title: Sub-keV nuclear-recoil ionization yield
open: How many electron–hole pairs does a sub-keV nuclear recoil actually produce in silicon and germanium, and what sets the threshold and orientation dependence of that yield? Conflicting measurements need to be reconciled through a recoil-energy calibration that is directly traceable.
status: The problem is decades old, with earlier yield measurements proving inconsistent. A 2024 Ge experiment revisited 254 eV nuclear recoils in this context: A. R. L. Kavner and I. Jovanovic (2024), [Measurement of ionization produced by 254 eV nuclear recoils in germanium](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.083043).
solved_when: Reproducible measurements of electron–hole production distributions for low-energy Si and Ge nuclear recoils — including thresholds and crystal-orientation effects — exist and the conflicting earlier results are explained by a traceable calibration.
why: The ionization yield directly controls how neutrino and light-dark-matter searches interpret their signals; without a settled yield, recoil-energy and cross-section inferences in these experiments remain ambiguous.
key_works: A. R. L. Kavner and I. Jovanovic (2024), [Measurement of ionization produced by 254 eV nuclear recoils in germanium](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.083043).

title: Nonmonotonic illumination drift in flexible IGZO
open: Can the anomalous reversal of threshold-voltage drift in flexible amorphous IGZO transistors — where drift changes sign under negative bias, illumination, and heating — be predicted from a physical model and suppressed in devices? In particular, can such a model be transferred across film thicknesses, illumination spectra, and display duty cycles?
status: A longstanding problem in oxide backplanes; 2025 work by D. Kim, K.-B. Lee, and B. Choi (2025), [Hydrogen and oxygen induced abnormal reliability degradation in flexible top-gate amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O thin-film transistors under negative bias thermal illumination stress](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2025.106902), linked the reversal to hydrogen/oxygen-associated states and suppressed it through thickness optimization.
solved_when: A validated model predicts the threshold-drift reversal under combined negative bias, illumination, and heating, and a suppression strategy demonstrably eliminates or substantially reduces the reversal across variations in thickness, spectrum, and duty cycle.
why: It prevents brightness drift during low-refresh display operation, which is essential for stable image quality in flexible oxide-backplane panels.
key_works: D. Kim, K.-B. Lee, and B. Choi (2025), [Hydrogen and oxygen induced abnormal reliability degradation in flexible top-gate amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O thin-film transistors under negative bias thermal illumination stress](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2025.106902).

title: Scandium segregation below the nominal phase boundary
open: Can nanoscale Sc-rich leakage paths in AlScN be suppressed while still preserving switchable wurtzite-phase material? More precisely, can precipitation be predicted from local composition fluctuations rather than from the average composition alone?
status: The problem was sharpened by 2025 observations of metallic rocksalt precipitates and enhanced leakage even at 10% Sc, reported in D. Wu et al. (2025), [Atomic Origins of Leakage Paths in Epitaxial Al1−xScxN Thin Films](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03675).
solved_when: A method or criterion is demonstrated that prevents nanoscale Sc-rich leakage paths below the nominal phase boundary while maintaining switchable wurtzite AlScN, with precipitation predicted from local composition fluctuations rather than average composition.
why: It connects ferroelectric switching with predictable insulation, so that the switching functionality no longer comes at the cost of dielectric breakdown.
key_works: D. Wu et al. (2025), [Atomic Origins of Leakage Paths in Epitaxial Al1−xScxN Thin Films](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03675).

title: Sub-10-nm low-resistance n-type contacts
open: Can ohmic electron injection be maintained reproducibly through contacts shorter than 10 nm in integrated top-gated TMD transistors while operating at logic voltages?
status: The problem has been central since the 2010s; in 2025, antimony contacts achieved 98 Ω·µm at an 18-nm contact length and 40-nm contacted gate pitch (M. Du et al. (2025), [Scaled crystalline antimony ohmic contacts for two-dimensional transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01500-4)).
solved_when: Sub-10-nm contacts in integrated top-gated TMD transistors show reproducible ohmic injection at logic voltages, improving on the current art of 98 Ω·µm at 18-nm contact length and 40-nm contacted gate pitch.
why: Otherwise contact resistance consumes the gains of device scaling, so smaller transistors no longer translate into better logic performance.
key_works: M. Du et al. (2025), [Scaled crystalline antimony ohmic contacts for two-dimensional transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01500-4).

title: Low-voltage 2D circuit speed beyond small oscillators
open: Can a large complementary two-dimensional-semiconductor circuit — with realistic wiring, fan-out, and leakage — demonstrate genuine speed and energy benefits over conventional logic at matched functionality and matched supply voltage? In other words, moving beyond small ring oscillators, can 2D logic be integrated at scale while retaining its advantages?
status: Circuit integration has lagged behind device-level results since the 2010s; the state of the art is five-stage MoS₂ oscillators reaching 2.65 GHz in 2023, per D. Fan et al. (2023), [Two-dimensional semiconductor integrated circuits operating at gigahertz frequencies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01052-5).
solved_when: A large complementary 2D-semiconductor circuit with realistic interconnect, fan-out, and leakage is demonstrated that outperforms a conventional circuit of identical functionality at the same supply voltage in both speed and energy.
why: Such a demonstration would establish 2D semiconductor logic as a useful computing technology rather than a laboratory curiosity.
key_works: D. Fan et al. (2023), [Two-dimensional semiconductor integrated circuits operating at gigahertz frequencies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01052-5).

title: Long-lived complementary CNT extension doping
open: Can carbon-nanotube transistors retain selective extension doping and well-matched complementary threshold voltages through fabrication processing and prolonged bias stress at scaled dimensions? Formally, the goal is a doping scheme whose complementary thresholds remain stable in operation rather than only at initial characterization.
status: Sought since the 2000s; in 2023, localized solid-state doping produced thresholds of +0.29 V and −0.25 V, per Z. Zhang et al. (2023), [Complementary carbon nanotube metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors with localized solid-state extension doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01047-2). A related physical-chemistry issue is charge-transfer ageing from defect configurations.
solved_when: Complementary CNT devices demonstrate selectively doped extensions with matched thresholds (+0.29 V and −0.25 V as the reference benchmarks) that persist through processing and sustained bias stress at scaled device dimensions.
why: Stable complementary thresholds are what make complementary CNT logic practical; without them, logic levels drift under operation.
key_works: Z. Zhang et al. (2023), [Complementary carbon nanotube metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors with localized solid-state extension doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01047-2).

title: Low-voltage ferroelectric tunnel-junction margins
open: Can a ferroelectric tunnel junction be made to deliver all of its headline virtues — large persistent electroresistance, low-voltage writing, high endurance, and uniformity over a small area — simultaneously in one operating regime, rather than trading one against another?
status: The problem has been explored since the 2000s. Junctions reported in 2024 achieved 1-nm barriers and billions of cycles, with contrast and endurance optimized under different pulses. Key work: Y. Jia et al. (2024), [Giant tunnelling electroresistance in atomic-scale ferroelectric tunnel junctions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-44927-7).
solved_when: A single junction design demonstrates, under one common set of operating pulses, a large persistent resistance contrast together with billions of write cycles, writing at low voltage, and uniform behavior at the 1-nm-barrier / small-area scale.
why: It would make extreme resistance ratios practically usable in real memory and in-memory-computing hardware instead of only under mutually exclusive operating conditions.
key_works: Y. Jia et al. (2024), [Giant tunnelling electroresistance in atomic-scale ferroelectric tunnel junctions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-44927-7).

title: Tenfold system-energy gain for autoregressive analogue inference
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Can autoregressive analogue inference hardware be made to deliver a full tenfold reduction in energy per generated token compared with matched digital hardware? The gain must hold at the system level, accounting for weight loading, nonlinear operations, and memory traffic, while matching digital quality and latency.
status: The field has been active since the 2010s. In 2023, analogue hardware demonstrated multi-chip speech inference with 45 million weights (S. Ambrogio et al. (2023), [An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5)).
solved_when: Energy per generated token, measured end-to-end (including loading, nonlinear operations, and memory traffic) on equal-quality, equal-latency autoregressive inference against matched digital hardware, is reduced tenfold.
why: Token generation is dominated by utilization and data-movement costs; a solution would remove the dominant energy bottleneck in autoregressive inference rather than just accelerating matrix multiplies.
key_works: S. Ambrogio et al. (2023), [An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5).

title: Sub-picojoule optical I/O including all overheads
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Can an optical I/O link deliver a bit for less than one picojoule once every overhead is paid for — lasers, drivers, receivers, tuning, coding, and idle power — under realistic traffic and temperature conditions? Formally, the goal is a complete optical I/O system whose total energy per delivered bit, measured across all of these components and overheads, falls below 1 pJ under realistic operating assumptions.
status: The problem has been actively pursued for over a decade. Wan and colleagues' 2025 review, "Integrating silicon photonics with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technologies" (https://doi.org/10.1038/s44287-025-00223-0), describes progress on components and co-design, but identifies sub-picojoule total-link energy and petabit integration as continuing system objectives.
solved_when: A demonstrated optical I/O system achieves total energy below one picojoule per delivered bit, with the accounting explicitly including lasers, drivers, receivers, tuning, coding, and idle overhead, under realistic traffic and temperatures.
why: It removes the communication-energy wall that currently constrains distributed computing, allowing interconnect energy to scale with compute rather than dominate system power budgets.
key_works: Wan et al. (2025, online), [*Integrating silicon photonics with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technologies*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44287-025-00223-0).

title: Tenfold lower EUV energy per yielding exposure
open: Can total electricity consumed per good patterned wafer layer be cut tenfold relative to a declared production baseline, while holding pitch, defect yield, and throughput requirements fixed?
status: ASML demonstrated a 1,000 W EUV source in April 2025, though its own account distinguishes that milestone from a commercial source, and optical power alone does not establish energy per good wafer. Related leverage lies in plasma physics, specifically efficient laser-to-radiation conversion. Key work: ASML (2026), [“Strategy & stories,” 2025 Annual Report](https://www.asml.com/en/investors/annual-report/2025/strategy-and-stories).
solved_when: A demonstrated process achieves a tenfold reduction in total energy per good patterned wafer layer against the declared production baseline, with pitch, defect yield, and throughput unchanged from that baseline.
why: A tenfold cut in energy per yielding exposure directly lowers operating cost and the environmental burden of continued lithographic scaling.
key_works: ASML (2026), [“Strategy & stories,” 2025 Annual Report](https://www.asml.com/en/investors/annual-report/2025/strategy-and-stories).

title: Tenfold reduction of electrically reset PCM energy
open: Can the RESET energy of electrically driven phase-change memory be reduced tenfold relative to a declared scaled baseline, while preserving speed, retention, read margin, and endurance, with contact losses fully accounted for?
status: Thermal-confinement research spans decades; in 2024, superlattice devices demonstrated approximately 0.7-V switching at 40-nm dimensions (X. Wu et al. (2024), [Novel nanocomposite-superlattices for low energy and high stability nanoscale phase-change memory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42792-4)).
solved_when: A PCM device demonstrates a tenfold reduction in electrical RESET energy against the declared scaled baseline while maintaining switching speed, retention, read margin, and endurance, and with contact losses included in the energy accounting.
why: Cutting the melt–quench energy cost directly lowers the operating energy of PCM, improving its competitiveness as a nonvolatile memory technology.
key_works: X. Wu et al. (2024), [Novel nanocomposite-superlattices for low energy and high stability nanoscale phase-change memory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42792-4).

title: Manufacturable sub-0.01-square-micrometre CFET SRAM
open: Can a CFET-based SRAM bitcell be manufactured at an area below 0.01 μm² per bitcell while remaining a genuinely usable memory — with adequate read/write margins, routable arrays, and statistically demonstrated yield?
status: This is a 2020s scaling target. Abdi's 2025 design–technology study predicts sub-0.01 μm² cells and improved write margins using wordline folding, rather than demonstrating a manufactured memory array.
solved_when: A sub-0.01 μm² CFET SRAM array is fabricated and measured, showing usable read/write margins, routable arrays, and demonstrated statistical yield, with local interconnect resistance and transistor mismatch reflected in the measured macro performance.
why: SRAM area scaling increasingly constrains cache capacity and processor cost; a manufacturable bitcell at this scale would directly relieve that constraint.
key_works: Dawit B. Abdi et al. (2025), [*SRAM Scaling Opportunities Below 0.01 μm² Using Double-Row CFET Architecture with Wordline-Folded Bitcell Design for Performance Optimization*](https://www.vlsisymposium.org/wp-content/uploads/VLSI2025_Advanceprogram0418.pdf).

title: High-temperature single-exposure dynamic range without noisy gain transitions
open: Can a pixel near 2 µm deliver, in a single exposure, a dynamic range above 130 dB at 125 °C without noisy gain transitions? Formally, this means flicker-free single-exposure operation with transition signal-to-noise ratio above 30 dB in approximately 2-µm pixels at that temperature.
status: Pursued since the 1990s. Innocent et al. (2025) reported 126-dB test-chip range in [*2.1µm LFM Automotive Pixel with Single Photodiode and 126 dB of Single Exposure Dynamic Range*](https://doi.org/10.60928/es6a-7h7l); their product target sacrificed range to preserve high-temperature transition quality.
solved_when: A single-exposure pixel design demonstrates dynamic range above 130 dB together with transition signal-to-noise ratio above 30 dB at 125 °C in approximately 2-µm pixels, without flicker from gain transitions.
why: It preserves automotive lamp and shadow detail, enabling robust perception under extreme illumination.
key_works: Innocent et al. (2025), [*2.1µm LFM Automotive Pixel with Single Photodiode and 126 dB of Single Exposure Dynamic Range*](https://doi.org/10.60928/es6a-7h7l).

title: Increasing-distance quantum error correction in silicon
open: Can a silicon spin-qubit device run repeated quantum error correction so that the logical error rate falls as the code distance grows — with leakage, measurement errors, and parallel operation all present rather than assumed away?
status: This goal has been pursued since early spin-qubit proposals. In 2026, donor clusters implemented a [[4,2,2]] detection code and shuttled spins performed weight-four parity checks, but scalable error suppression remains unestablished. Key works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Universal logical operations in a silicon quantum processor*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-026-02140-1); Undseth et al. (2026), [*Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10766-3).
solved_when: A silicon experiment demonstrates error correction at increasing code distances, showing logical error rates that decrease with distance under realistic conditions including leakage, measurement errors, and parallel operation.
why: It converts high-quality physical spins into dependable computational resources; without scalable error suppression, silicon qubits cannot serve as building blocks of a fault-tolerant machine.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Universal logical operations in a silicon quantum processor*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-026-02140-1); Undseth et al. (2026), [*Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10766-3).
